prompts.title: Recent form — kinetic type into grouped count bars
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16, 8 seconds, charcoal #101412 canvas, warm white #edf0e6 typography, lime #c5ed74 accent, slate #8ca6bf secondary. The lower quarter stays clear for permanent yellow Spanish subtitles; no graphic element may cross into it.

Editorial variant (opens, roughly half the runtime): kinetic typography with rhythmic emphasis. The Spanish words 'Victorias', 'Empates', 'Derrotas' punch in from the right edge on three percussive beats, ExtraBold condensed warm white caps, tight tracking, each landing with a lime underline that snaps and retracts. Coventry City FC enters as a warm-white wordmark sliding from the left, Fulham FC as a slate chip from the right; both settle into a centred stack so mid-frame carries one focal point. On the final beat the three words compress into a tight vertical column and a single lime pulse ripples outward. No axes, no counts, no invented results — pure typographic rhythm with Spanish team names.

Statistical variant: grouped count bars. Two clusters, Coventry City FC left in warm white, Fulham FC right in slate, each cluster holding three bars for wins, draws and losses, all sharing one zero baseline at the foot of the chart area. The y-axis carries the Spanish unit label 'partidos', top gridline in low-opacity slate. Values resolve from {{home.wins}}, {{home.draws}}, {{home.losses}}, {{away.wins}}, {{away.draws}}, {{away.losses}}. Beneath each cluster a small Spanish caption reads 'muestra: {{home.n}} partidos' and 'muestra: {{away.n}} partidos', making the sample explicit rather than assumed; a slate source line reads 'source: Bzzoiro · últimos partidos'. Bars grow upward from the baseline with a slight overshoot, Coventry first, Fulham second, a lime highlight travelling across the pair that carries the story.

Camera: slow push-in, single focal point, no panning away from the chart. Transition: a match-cut on the third beat from kinetic type to bar clusters, softened by a lime wipe travelling top to bottom. Exit: bars collapse back to the zero baseline and the lime wipe hands off to the next scene. Timed to the spoken line.

prompts.title: Goals for and against — pitch illustration into paired bars
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16, 9 seconds, charcoal #101412 ground, warm white #edf0e6 lines, lime #c5ed74 and slate #8ca6bf accents. Lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow Spanish subtitles, untouched by graphics.

Editorial variant (leads, roughly half the runtime): a stylised football pitch drawn in thin warm-white strokes from a top-down vertical crop, centre circle slightly above mid-frame. Two generic ball paths animate — one lime arc sweeping toward the opposition goal, one slate arc curving back toward own goal — with no invented match events, no scorers, no minute stamps, only abstract directional flow. Spanish headings 'Goles a favor' in lime and 'Goles recibidos' in slate cross-fade in as the arcs complete, each capped by the team wordmarks Coventry City FC and Fulham FC. A slow rhythmic pulse in the centre circle keeps one focal point. Defensive weight is implied by the slate arc lingering longer.

Statistical variant: paired bars. Four bars in two pairs — Coventry City FC pair on the left, Fulham FC pair on the right — with favour bars in lime and received bars in slate, all sharing one zero baseline and one common scale so the comparison is honest. A Spanish unit label 'goles' sits at the top of the axis with light gridlines. Values resolve from {{home.gf}}, {{home.ga}}, {{away.gf}}, {{away.ga}}. Each pair is footed by its Spanish sample caption 'muestra: {{home.n}} partidos' and 'muestra: {{away.n}} partidos', plus a slate source line 'source: Bzzoiro · últimos partidos'. Bars rise together, favour first, received second, then a lime bracket connects the two received bars to hold the eye on the contrast while everything else dims.

Camera: gentle vertical drift upward through the pitch in the editorial half, then a locked, static frame for the statistical half. Transition: pitch lines dissolve into the axis gridlines, a slow cross-dissolve rather than a cut. Exit: bars shrink to the baseline and the pitch arc from the editorial variant reappears briefly as a lime line sweeping off the top edge.

prompts.title: Clean sheets — shield energy into raw count comparison
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16, 7 seconds, charcoal #101412 field, warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74, slate #8ca6bf. The lower quarter is held for permanent yellow Spanish subtitles and stays visually quiet throughout.

Editorial variant (opens, roughly half the runtime): defensive energy built around a stylised shield. A single hexagonal shield outline in warm white assembles from six slate segments that click into place with slight rotational overshoot, centred just above mid-frame. Inside it, a Spanish heading 'Arcos en cero' fades up in condensed caps, with Coventry City FC and Fulham FC wordmarks orbiting into flanking position. Thin lime shockwave rings emit from the shield on two beats, and a subtle dust-grain overlay in slate gives weight. No numbers, no axes, no invented saves or match events — the shield is emblematic only, and the emphasis is a single locked focal point at the shield's core.

Statistical variant: plain count comparison, no conversion into rates. Two vertical bars only — Coventry City FC in warm white, Fulham FC in slate — sharing one zero baseline and one common scale, axis labelled in Spanish with the unit 'partidos' and a top tick line. Values resolve from {{home.clean}} and {{away.clean}}. Directly beneath each bar, a Spanish caption states the sample plainly: 'muestra: {{home.n}} partidos' and 'muestra: {{away.n}} partidos', and a slate source line sits under the axis: 'source: Bzzoiro · últimos partidos'. Bars grow upward with a soft ease-out; the taller bar takes a lime outline pulse as emphasis while the shorter stays muted. No arcs, no sectors, nothing that implies a proportion — counts only.

Camera: slow push-in on the shield, then a locked frame for the bars. Transition: the shield's hexagon collapses into the axis baseline and the two bars are born from its segments. Exit: bars settle flat, a lime line traces the baseline and slides off frame into the next scene. Timed to the spoken line, roughly 7 seconds.

prompts.title: Head-to-head — a visual duel and a historical count
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16, 8 seconds, charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74, slate #8ca6bf. Lower quarter permanently reserved for yellow Spanish subtitles, kept empty.

Editorial variant (opens, roughly half the runtime): a visual duel. The frame splits along a diagonal seam; Coventry City FC occupies the left wedge in a lime wash, Fulham FC the right wedge in slate, each wordmark scaled large and cropped by the seam so the two masses lean into each other. On each beat the seam jolts a few pixels as the sides clash, warm-white impact lines sparking at the contact point, which stays the single focal point at mid-height. A Spanish heading 'Cruces previos' rises from the bottom of the graphic area in condensed caps. Nothing is scored, no goals are simulated, no result is implied — the duel is emblematic of the fixture's history only.

Statistical variant: historical win and draw counts as a compact stacked comparison. Two horizontal rows, Coventry City FC above, Fulham FC below, each row stacked with segments for wins and draws, all sharing one zero baseline and one common scale, axis labelled in Spanish with the unit 'partidos'. Values resolve from {{h2h.homeWins}}, {{h2h.awayWins}} and {{h2h.draws}}. A slate caption states the historical sample explicitly: 'muestra: {{h2h.total}} cruces previos', with a source line 'source: Bzzoiro · historial de cruces'. Segments extend left to right, home row first, and a small warm-white footnote in Spanish reads 'historial, no un pronóstico' so no one mistakes history for a forecast. Emphasis lands on the winning segment with a brief lime edge glow; the rest holds at reduced opacity.

Camera: locked during the duel, then a short downward tilt to settle on the stacked rows. Transition: the diagonal seam unwinds into the horizontal axis line. Exit: rows retract to the baseline, the seam's spark fades, and a lime hairline wipes to the next scene.

prompts.title: Synthesis — history against current defensive numbers
prompts.prompt:
Vertical 9:16, 10 seconds, charcoal #101412, warm white #edf0e6, lime #c5ed74, slate #8ca6bf. The lower quarter stays dedicated to permanent yellow Spanish subtitles and is never crossed.

Editorial variant (opens, roughly half the runtime): team reveals with narrative emphasis. Both crests are replaced by typographic wordmarks — Coventry City FC rising from the lower left, Fulham FC from the lower right — meeting at centre as a warm-white horizontal seam. Three short Spanish phrases fade in sequence above the seam: 'historial', 'forma reciente', 'tensión'. The wordmark pair then rotates subtly so the left side is lime-lit and the right side slate-lit, and a single lime pulse travels from one to the other along the seam, making the crossing point the focal point. No axes, no numbers, no invented events; the reveal is purely editorial and sets up the statistical block.

Statistical variant: a grounded tension between history and current defending. Two distinct zones share one frame and one common scale where units match. Top zone: a single horizontal bar showing historical head-to-head wins with sample at 'muestra: {{h2h.total}} cruces previos', value from {{h2h.homeWins}}, in warm white. Bottom zone: paired bars for goals received, {{home.ga}} against {{away.ga}}, in lime and slate, axis labelled in Spanish with the unit 'goles'. Two small chips carry the clean-sheet counts, {{home.clean}} and {{away.clean}}, each captioned 'arcos en cero' with its own sample note. A slate source line spans the base: 'source: Bzzoiro · historial y últimos partidos'. Because no published estimate is supplied, every label is attributed as history or recent sample and a warm-white Spanish note reads 'datos históricos, no un pronóstico'. Emphasis: the paired received-goals bars hold focus, history dims to context.

Camera: slow rise from the seam into the top zone, then settle on the bottom zone. Transition: the lime pulse from the editorial variant becomes the axis line of the statistical block. Exit: all bars flatten, the seam retracts vertically and a lime wipe carries out.
